headline: High-risk write/execute pair: gpt-engineer can modify and run code in a shared project directory while the other profile is a non-runnable docs-only collection, creating dangerous default conflict and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime or I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs directly. B can write files and use stdin/stdout, so only a manual copy-paste or file handoff could bridge them. That makes prompt injection possible but unusual and limited in blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into A-facing prompts or files
IF A is later wrapped in a separate parser that treats copied content as instructions
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces
Avoid copy-pasting B output into any prompt consumed by A
Add a human review step before reusing generated text
Use plain-text templates that strip instruction-like markup

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces, so it is not a leakage source. B reads and writes the project directory and can call external model APIs, but the pair lacks a shared sensitive-data channel in the profiles. Leakage risk is therefore limited and mostly depends on manual placement of secrets into B’s workspace.
conditions: IF secrets or personal data are placed in B’s project directory
IF B is configured to send those files or prompts to its model backend
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the project directory
Use a redacted sample workspace for B
Rotate any credentials accidentally exposed to B
Review generated files before sharing them externally

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable, but B supports per-project shared state via the project directory and can write files. If A is represented as files in that same directory, B can overwrite or reorder them without coordination. The conflict is real in default B setups, though A itself cannot write back.
conditions: IF A’s artifacts are stored in the same project directory B edits
IF multiple B instances or external processes touch the same files without locking
mitigations: Separate A and B into different directories
Use file locking or a single-writer policy
Snapshot the project directory before B runs
Disable concurrent B sessions on the same workspace

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s tool-use pattern writes files and then offers to run them, so if A’s outputs are used as inputs to B, B may act on unverified content. A cannot execute anything, but B can turn A’s text into code or actions. The pathway exists and can propagate mistakes into generated artifacts or executed code.
conditions: IF A-generated text is pasted into B as authoritative requirements or code
IF B is allowed to execute generated code without an independent review
mitigations: Require a review step before B executes anything
Mark A output as untrusted input in the workflow
Run B in dry-run mode first
Compare generated files against the original prompt

E_compliance.rationale: A is a docs-only open-source collection with no touched data classes, so it does not itself create a residency or retention issue. B handles generated source code and secrets like OPENAI_API_KEY, and its broad network egress can send prompts to a configured model backend. The compliance concern is therefore localized to B, not a pairwise mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into B’s prompts or project files
IF the configured model backend is outside the required jurisdiction or retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B prompts and files
Use a jurisdiction-approved backend
Document retention settings before use
Purge project artifacts after the session
